title: Large Language Models for Machine Translation Quality Annotation: Humans and Models Are Both Challenged
gist: Apple researchers compare LLM and human annotators on machine translation quality (MQM and ESA schemes) across 70 language pairs plus WMT23 and WMT25 data. LLM agreement sometimes exceeds human-human agreement, but both are unreliable in most settings, pointing toward human-LLM collaborative annotation.

insights.claim: LLMs are considered a more efficient and cost-effective alternative to human judgment for machine translation evaluation, but must be tested across language pairs, domains and annotation granularities before reliable substitution.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: LLM-as-judge cost savings depend on validation that this work finds lacking.

insights.claim: The study compares LLM and human agreement for two schemes, Multidimensional Quality Metrics (MQM) and Error Span Annotation (ESA), on a long-context test set of 70 language pairs and public WMT23 and WMT25 data.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Scale of 70 language pairs makes the reliability finding broadly credible.
insights.locator: we evaluate the performance of LLMs

insights.claim: LLM agreement with human annotators exceeds agreement between human annotators for some evaluation tasks, yet both vary substantially across schemes, language pairs and domains and remain unreliable for most settings.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Human annotation is not a clean gold standard; benchmark noise limits both training and evaluation signal.

themes.theme: Failure modes of humans and LLMs

insights.claim: Human annotators are particularly challenged by fine-grained MQM annotations and low-resource language pairs.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Low-resource languages are where evaluation data is weakest and AI quality hardest to verify.

insights.claim: LLM annotators struggle with minor errors, wrong language variants and error span annotation.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Subtle translation errors can slip through automated QA; limits fully automated localization quality control.

insights.claim: The authors suggest that human-LLM collaborative annotation pipelines may address the reliability issues, so improvement potential exists for both annotator types.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Hybrid annotation pipelines may remain a demand source for human annotation despite LLM automation.
insights.locator: possibly through human-LLM collaborative annotation pipelines

themes.theme: Annotation quality in related Apple work

insights.claim: Related Apple work holds that safety-annotation disagreement can come from operational failures, policy ambiguity or value pluralism, and that distinguishing these matters.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Disagreement is not always noise; it can reflect ambiguous policy or real value differences.

insights.claim: Related Apple work trained a predictive error model to detect annotation errors in search relevance tasks for three industry-scale ML applications including music and video streaming.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Data-quality tooling is an operational cost center in production ML.
insights.locator: This paper presents a predictive error model
